ir13_documents.topic: A Clean Break (1996) and the Yinon essay (1982): what they say, especially about Iran

claims.text: A Clean Break was published 1 June 1996 by the Institute for Advanced Strategic and Political Studies (IASPS), written for incoming PM Netanyahu by its 'Study Group on a New Israeli Strategy Toward 2000': Richard Perle (leader), James Colbert, Charles Fairbanks Jr., Douglas Feith, Jonathan Torop, David Wurmser, Meyrav Wurmser, Robert Loewenberg (IASPS president).

The paper's text mentions Iran three times: Israel could seize the initiative on its northern borders 'by engaging Hizballah, Syria, and Iran, as the principal agents of aggression in Lebanon'; 'Syria recently signaled that it and Iran might prefer a weak, but barely surviving Saddam'; Hashemites controlling Iraq could help Israel 'wean the south Lebanese Shia away from Hizballah, Iran, and Syria.'

Its central recommendations: shape the strategic environment with Turkey and Jordan 'by weakening, containing, and even rolling back Syria', focusing on 'removing Saddam Hussein from power in Iraq'; 'striking Syrian military targets in Lebanon' and, should that prove insufficient, targets in Syria; Israel 'has the opportunity to make a clean break'; steps to terminate US economic aid and loan guarantees.

Feith: 'I was not a co-author of the "Clean Break" paper. I neither wrote it nor signed it'; principal author was David Wurmser; IASPS described the participants as a study group; Feith says his contribution was the idea that Israel 'graduate' from US economic aid.

Interpretations: Whitaker (Guardian 2002) said the plan looked more achievable with authors in Washington posts; Buchanan (2003) said it was imposed on the US; Mearsheimer and Walt said it called for Israel to reorder the Middle East; CBS's David Martin (2005) never saw evidence Perle had a determining effect on US policy; Netanyahu rejected some of its policies.

Oded Yinon's 'A Strategy for Israel in the 1980s' appeared in Kivunim (Feb 1982), a Hebrew quarterly of the World Zionist Organization's Department of Information; Yinon reputedly a former Foreign Ministry official and Jerusalem Post journalist; Israel Shahak's English translation circulated from June 1982, also titled 'The Zionist Plan for the Middle East'.

Yinon argued for fragmenting Arab states into ethnic and confessional units: Iraq split into Shiite, Sunni and Kurdish centres; Syria to 'fall apart ... into several states'; Egypt a 'corpse'; Jordan's 'liquidation'. Iran appears only twice, both as the Iran-Iraq war ('An Iraqi-Iranian war will tear Iraq apart').

Scholars' views: Nisan said the views were Yinon's alone, not policy; Harkabi found the analysis of Arab weaknesses 'generally correct' but questioned interference; Peleg called it 'an authentic mirror of the thinking mode of the Israeli Right'; Chomsky called its views 'ideological and geopolitical fantasies' not mainstream; Becker and Polkinghorn (2017) argue it was refined in A Clean Break; conspiracy theories claim it planned the Iraq invasion, Syrian war and ISIS.

claims.text: Israeli government statement after the Osirak strike (7 June 1981): 'On no account shall we permit an enemy to develop weapons of mass destruction against the people of Israel'; Begin at a press conference: 'We shall not allow any enemy to develop weapons of mass destruction turned against us'; said it 'will be a precedent for every future government in Israel'.

UNSC Resolution 487 (19 June 1981), adopted unanimously, 'Strongly condemns the military attack by Israel in clear violation of the Charter of the United Nations and the norms of international conduct' and 'Calls upon Israel urgently to place its nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards'.

On 21 March 2018 Israel's military acknowledged it destroyed a Syrian reactor at Deir ez-Zor on 6 September 2007; Eisenkot: 'Israel will not tolerate construction that can pose an existential threat'; 'This was the message in 1981, this is the message in 2007'; AP noted it could be read as a warning to Iran.

Yadlin (former head of military intelligence, an Osirak pilot), INSS March 2018: doctrine holds hostile states calling for Israel's destruction 'must not be allowed to develop a nuclear military capability'; may not be 'eternally viable' because Iran's centrifuge programme 'can be dispersed, concealed, and protected more effectively'; a strike can only postpone a determined programme and 'the attack itself might accelerate the effort'.

ir13_aims.topic: Israel's stated aims toward Iran, 2025-2026, incl. regime change

claims.text: June 2025: Israel's stated war aims were eliminating Iran's nuclear and ballistic-missile capabilities; Israeli officials told Axios regime change was not among security-cabinet objectives. Netanyahu, Fox News 15 June, suggested the war could lead to a change of government; ABC 16 June on killing Khamenei: 'It's not going to escalate the conflict, it's going to end the conflict'; 16 June to Israeli reporters: 'we could see many changes in Iran.'

Netanyahu statement, 28 Feb 2026: 'The aim of the operation is to put an end to the threat from the Ayatollah regime in Iran'; 'if we do not act, we will face a nuclear Iran, an Iran with tens of thousands of ballistic missiles'; of 2025 regime change 'I replied that this was not the goal, but it could certainly be the outcome'; now to 'create conditions that will allow the brave Iranian people to cast off the yoke of this murderous regime'; 'You are not our enemies and we are not your enemies'; 'For 47 years, the evil regime in Iran has called for death to Israel, death to America.'

ir13_explanations.topic: Analysts' explanations for the Israel-Iran rivalry (arguments)

claims.text: Parsi (Treacherous Alliance, 2007) argues the Israel-Iran rivalry is 'neither about ideology nor religion' but geopolitics; after Iraq's defeat in the early 1990s 'Israeli politicians began describing Iran as the primary threat'; Scowcroft is quoted that 'The pro-Israeli community turned strongly against Iran'.

Sadjadpour (2018): opposition to Israel is 'the most enduring pillar of Iranian revolutionary ideology', a 'visceral and seemingly inextinguishable hatred', not driven by national interests; quotes Khamenei: 'The Zionist regime is a true cancer tumor on this region that should be cut off' (2012) and that Israel 'will not be in existence in 25 years'.

June 2025: the war gave Netanyahu political breathing room after a coalition crisis and failed dissolution push, amid his corruption trial; analyst Nimrod Flaschenberg: 'The idea that Iran is the source of all evil has become embedded across Israeli society'; Dov Waxman called it a 'big gamble'; opposition leader Lapid backed the strikes and Bennett said 'There is no right, no left, no opposition and no coalition'.

As of November 2023, 30 of 193 UN member states did not recognise Israel; in the Middle East these included Iran (which withdrew relations) and Iraq, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Yemen (never recognised).
SIPRI: Israel supplied 27% of Azerbaijan's major arms imports in 2011-20, rising to 69% in 2016-20; Russia about 60% over 2011-20.

World Bank: Iran's GDP contracted an estimated 2.7% in 2025/26 (year to 20 March 2026).
SIPRI: 2025 military expenditure Iran $7.4bn (38th); Israel $48.3bn (11th, 7.8% of GDP); Saudi Arabia $83.2bn; Turkey $30.0bn; US $954bn.

SIPRI via New Arab: Iran's 2025 spending fell 5.6% in real terms, second annual decline, mostly due to 42% inflation; allocations to HESA (aircraft/drones) rose 50% and AIO (ballistic missiles) 44%; budgeted figures 'probably represent only a relatively small proportion of Iran's procurement spending'; Israel down 4.9% but 120% above 2016; Israel received $3.8bn US military aid in 2025; Middle East total $218bn.

EIA: about 20 million b/d of oil, about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption, passed through Hormuz in 2024, plus about one-fifth of global LNG trade; 84% of the crude and 83% of the LNG went to Asia; Saudi and UAE pipelines could offer about 2.6 million b/d of bypass.

ir13_forces.topic: Power ledger: forces, missiles, US presence

claims.text: IISS Military Balance 2025 (via NST): Iran about 610,000 active personnel, IRGC about 190,000; about 250 combat-capable aircraft, many predating 1979 incl. F-4, F-5 and a small number of F-14s; pre-June-2025 missile estimates 2,500-3,000 (unattributed).

Alma (Israeli research centre): 13-24 June 2025 Iran launched 525 ballistic missiles at Israel; about 86% intercepted; 50-60 struck the home front; over 1,000 drones, ~99% intercepted; 28 civilians killed, 1,472 injured.

FDD (May 2026): IDF estimated about 2,500 missiles able to reach Israel at the start of the 2026 war; Iran launched roughly 2,200-2,400 missiles in four waves 2024-2026; Israeli Air Force official (5 April 2026): just over 1,000 remain; Israel Hayom (3 Apr): about half of launchers intact; NYT (12 May, classified US assessment): Iran retained roughly 70% of prewar missile stockpile (apparently incl. cruise missiles); CENTCOM's Cooper: over 85% of the missile, drone and naval defence industrial base damaged or destroyed, called NYT/WaPo reports 'not accurate'.
Al Jazeera: about 40,000-50,000 US troops in the Middle East as of mid-2025 at at least 19 sites (CFR), eight permanent; Al Udeid about 10,000; NSA Bahrain about 9,000 (Fifth Fleet).
NYT (30 Mar 2026): more than 50,000 US troops in the region, up from a usual level of around 40,000, per a US military official.

ir13_audit.topic: Audit re-verification of Part Thirteen document and figure claims (October 2026)

claims.text: A Clean Break mentions Iran in four sentences: 'engaging Hizballah, Syria, and Iran, as the principal agents of aggression in Lebanon'; Syria 'and Iran might prefer a weak, but barely surviving Saddam'; south Lebanese Shia tied to 'the Shia leadership in Najf, Iraq rather than Iran'; Hashemites could help 'wean the south Lebanese Shia away from Hizballah, Iran, and Syria'

The monabaker.org copy of Yinon's essay is incomplete (ends with the Arabian peninsula paragraph; lacks Jordan section and notes); in that text Iran appears in two sentences, both on the Iran-Iraq war; translator's note says Shahak's translation was disseminated on 13 June 1982, a week after Israel invaded Lebanon
SIPRI research assistant Zubaida Karim estimated Iran's off-budget military spending at about 40% of the total
